caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: Диаграмата представя сравнение на перплексията при две конфигурации на подрязване — „Per-Output" (в синьо) и „Per-Layer" (в оранжево) — при различни нива на разреденост (sparsity rate). Хоризонталната ос е означена като „Sparsity Rate" и съдържа категории, подредени в нарастващ ред от 10% до 80% с интервал от 10 процентни пункта. Вертикалната ос е означена като „Perplexity" и използва логаритмична скала, обхващаща диапазон от приблизително 10⁰ до 10³, с пунктирани хоризонтални линии при стойности 10¹, 10² и 10³. За всяка категория на разреденост са представени два стълба — син за „Per-Output" и оранжев за „Per-Layer", разположени един до друг. При нива на разреденост от 10% до 50% и двата стълба остават с ниски стойности, под 10¹, като разликите между тях са визуално минимални. При 60% разреденост стълбовете започват да нарастват забележимо, като синият стълб достига приблизително 15, а оранжевият остава близо до 10¹. При 70% синият стълб се издига до приблизително 50, а оранжевият — до около 25–35. При 80% разреденост и двата стълба достигат стойности, приближаващи се към 10³, като синият стълб е с незначително по-голяма височина от оранжевия. Легендата е разположена в горния ляв ъгъл на диаграмата и обозначава двете серии данни чрез цветни квадратчета. Стълбовете не са допълнително подчертани чрез засенчване, очертаване или анотации.
raw_responses.Chinese:
Let me analyze the visual structure of this figure step by step.

**Chart type:** Grouped bar chart with two data series per category.

**Axes:**
- Horizontal axis: Sparsity Rate (categorical, from 10% to 80%)
- Vertical axis: Perplexity, on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 5 to 10³

**Data series:** Two series — "Per-Output" (blue) and "Per-Layer" (orange), as shown in the legend.

**Patterns:** At low sparsity rates, both bars are nearly identical and small. As sparsity increases beyond 50%, the bars grow dramatically, with the blue (Per-Output) bars generally taller than the orange (Per-Layer) bars at 60% and 70%, but at 80% the orange bar appears slightly taller.

Wait — the caption says at 80% Per-Output has marginally higher perplexity, but visually the orange bar looks slightly taller at 80%. Let me re-examine... The blue bar at 80% reaches roughly 500-600 and the orange bar reaches roughly 800-900. Actually, looking more carefully, the caption notes both approach 10³ with Per-Output marginally higher — but visually the orange bar appears taller at 80%.

DESCRIPTION: This grouped bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations — Per-Output (blue) and Per-Layer (orange) — across eight sparsity rate categories on the horizontal axis: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis represents Perplexity on a logarithmic scale, with gridlines at approximately 10⁰·⁷ (roughly 5), 10¹, 10², and 10³, spanning a range from just below 10¹ to 10³. For each sparsity rate, two bars are placed side by side, with the blue (Per-Output) bar on the left and the orange (Per-Layer) bar on the right. At sparsity rates of 10% through 30%, both bars are nearly identical in height, each registering values close to approximately 5, just below the 10¹ gridline. At 40% sparsity, both bars remain very similar, with values slightly above 5. At 50% sparsity, the bars begin to show a slight increase, with both still below 10¹. At 60% sparsity, the bars become visibly taller, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 15 and the orange Per-Layer bar near 10¹ (approximately 10–12). At 70% sparsity, the separation becomes more pronounced, with the blue bar climbing to roughly 20 and the orange bar reaching approximately 35–40. At 80% sparsity, both bars rise dramatically toward 10³, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 500–600 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 800–900. The bars are ordered by increasing sparsity rate from left to right, and no bars are visually emphasized through special shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the standard color coding indicated in the legend positioned in the upper left area of the chart.
raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: This chart compares perplexity values for two pruning configurations—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across different sparsity rates, displayed as a grouped bar chart. The horizontal axis represents the Sparsity Rate, with categories labeled at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis represents Perplexity, plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 1 to 10³, with dashed horizontal gridlines at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. Each sparsity rate has two bars side by side: a blue bar representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar representing "Per-Layer," as indicated by the legend in the upper left corner. At 10%, 20%, and 30% sparsity, both blue and orange bars are very short and nearly identical in height, with perplexity values close to approximately 5. At 40% sparsity, the bars remain similar and slightly taller, still below 10¹. At 50%, both bars are marginally taller but remain near or just below 10¹. At 60% sparsity, the blue Per-Output bar reaches approximately 15 while the orange Per-Layer bar is slightly shorter at roughly 10–12. At 70%, the separation becomes more pronounced, with the blue bar reaching approximately 20–50 and the orange bar at roughly 25–35. At 80% sparsity, both bars grow dramatically, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 500–600 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 800–900, both approaching 10³. The bars are not sorted independently but follow the natural ascending order of sparsity rates, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized through outlining or annotation beyond the standard color coding.
raw_responses.German: DESCRIPTION: Das Diagramm vergleicht die Perplexität zweier Pruning-Konfigurationen – „Per-Output" und „Per-Layer" – bei unterschiedlichen Sparsity-Raten und verwendet dabei eine logarithmische Skala auf der vertikalen Achse. Die horizontale Achse trägt die Beschriftung „Sparsity Rate" und zeigt acht Kategorien in aufsteigender Reihenfolge: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% und 80%. Die vertikale Achse ist mit „Perplexity" beschriftet und verwendet eine logarithmische Skala, die von etwa 10⁰ (unterhalb von 10¹) bis 10³ reicht, mit gestrichelten Hilfslinien bei 10¹, 10² und 10³. Für jede Sparsity-Rate sind zwei Balken nebeneinander gruppiert dargestellt: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output" (links) und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer" (rechts), wie in der Legende oben links angegeben. Bei den Sparsity-Raten 10%, 20% und 30% erreichen beide Balken jeweils sehr niedrige Werte knapp unterhalb von 10¹, wobei die Höhen nahezu identisch erscheinen (ungefähr 5). Bei 40% steigen die Werte leicht an, bleiben aber weiterhin unter 10¹. Bei 50% liegen beide Balken noch im Bereich knapp unter oder um 10¹. Bei 60% erreicht der blaue „Per-Output"-Balken einen Wert von etwa 15, während der orangefarbene „Per-Layer"-Balken bei ungefähr 10¹ verbleibt. Bei 70% steigt der blaue Balken auf etwa 50 und der orangefarbene auf ungefähr 25–35. Bei 80% nähern sich beide Balken dem Bereich von 10³, wobei der blaue „Per-Output"-Balken geringfügig höher als der orangefarbene „Per-Layer"-Balken erscheint, mit Werten von etwa 600 bzw. 900. Die Balken sind nicht explizit sortiert, sondern folgen der natürlichen aufsteigenden Reihenfolge der Sparsity-Raten, und es sind keine besonderen visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Umrandungen oder Annotationen an einzelnen Balken vorhanden.
